title: Summer Camp Story Circle Kit - Lower Activity Lane

activities.title: Teacup Town Weather Window
activities.sessionFit: 15-minute morning story circle for young writers who can choose one weather clue and one helpful action.
activities.counselorSetup: Print one page per kid, set out pencils, and pick a pretend weather card before circle begins.
activities.kidDirection: Look through the tiny weather window, choose what changes outside, and finish the three story parts.
activities.counselorPrompt: Ask which weather clue is easiest to picture, then invite one simple because sentence.

pageSections.heading: Weather Window
lines: Outside the teacup window, the weather looks like ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Town Helper
lines: The helper checks the sky near ____________________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: Pass the pretend weather card and let each writer add one sky detail: ____________________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The weather detail I used best was ____________________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: circle one line to finish later: ____________________________.

activities.title: Rain Gauge Railway
activities.sessionFit: 15-minute transition activity for a lower group that needs first, next, and last story steps.
activities.counselorSetup: Print one page per kid, draw three pretend train stops on scrap paper, and model one short route aloud.
activities.kidDirection: Choose a rain-gauge ticket, send the tiny train to three stops, and finish the route sentence.
activities.counselorPrompt: Point to each stop and ask what happens first, next, and last before writing.

pageSections.heading: Railway Stops
lines: Next, the gauge marker rises to ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Route Message
lines: The conductor says the route is calm because ____________________________.
The best stop for a story clue is ____________________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: Group twist: build a three-stop route aloud and write the stop you like most: ____________________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The order word that helped my story was ____________________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: draw one tiny rail mark, then fill this clue: ____________________________.

activities.title: Spoon Ferry Lunchbox Harbor
activities.sessionFit: 15-minute picnic-table story circle for kids who can pick a harbor object and describe where it goes.
activities.counselorSetup: Print one page per kid, place a pretend spoon ferry marker in the middle, and invite one quiet look before writing.
activities.kidDirection: Send the spoon ferry across the lunchbox harbor, choose what it carries, and finish the harbor note.
activities.counselorPrompt: Ask which harbor object belongs near the ferry, then ask what the ferry carries next.

pageSections.heading: Lunchbox Harbor
lines: The harbor flag is made from ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Ferry Load
lines: The ferry carries a pretend picnic of ____________________________.
The careful ferry path goes around ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Harbor Note
lines: Next, the harbor crew listens for ____________________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: Group twist: each writer adds one pretend harbor sound before choosing a line: ____________________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The harbor object I described clearly was ____________________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: finish only the ferry load line first: ____________________________.

activities.title: Rain Boot Route Rangers
activities.sessionFit: 20-minute story circle for a lower group ready to combine direction words with a small helpful route.
activities.counselorSetup: Print one page per kid, sketch a three-step pretend trail, and offer beside, under, past, or around as choices.
activities.kidDirection: Choose two rain-boot clues, map the route, and write where the route rangers go first.
activities.counselorPrompt: Ask the group to point in the air for beside, under, past, or around, then choose one word for writing.

pageSections.heading: Boot Map
lines: The left rain boot points toward ____________________________.
The right rain boot holds a map of ____________________________.

pageSections.heading: Path Clues
lines: The first puddle clue is beside ____________________________.
The second route mark hides under ____________________________.
The last dry stepping spot is ____________________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: Group twist: choose one direction word and use it in this route clue: ____________________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The map clue that made my route clearer was ____________________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: trace the route with a finger, then finish this line: ____________________________.

activities.title: Pocket Park Notice Board
activities.sessionFit: 20-minute closing circle for writers who can make a pretend notice and explain why it helps the pocket park.
activities.counselorSetup: Print one page per kid, show three blank pretend notice strips, and remind the circle to use invented park details.
activities.kidDirection: Invent a pocket park notice, choose the clearest reason, and write what the park helper does next.
activities.counselorPrompt: Ask kids to keep notices invented and place-based, then help them finish one because line.

pageSections.heading: Notice Board
lines: The first pocket park notice asks for ____________________________.
The board frame is decorated with ____________________________.

activities.groupTwistLine: Group twist: share one pretend park object and add it to this notice: ____________________________.
activities.wrapUpLine: The reason that makes my notice useful is ____________________________.
activities.quietOptionLine: Quiet option: choose one notice to copy neatly here: ____________________________.
